title: normalize-tool-schema-annotations-and-introduce-stream-heartbeat-for-fragment-coalescing
author: Priya Nandakumar
description: Context: We have several compatibility edge cases when bridging OpenAI-style function/tool-calling into Redwood's native invoke pipeline. Two concrete problems surfaced in customer integrations: 1) clients sending tool schemas with inconsistent property annotations (e.g., nested 'required' declared both on object and individual properties) which causes downstream schema resolution to fail, and 2) long-running fragment coalescing during streaming function/tool handoffs can cause client-side timeouts. This PR introduces: 1) a tool schema normalization pass (v3) that canonicalizes required/nullable/enum annotations, flattens aliasing for common types, and preserves vendor extensions in a provenance header; 2) a runtime-safe streaming "heartbeat" envelope injected between fragments when coalescing is delayed beyond the configured fragment window, keeping HTTP/WS clients alive without leaking semantic tokens; 3) an opt-in OpenAI compatibility header OpenAI-Compat: tool-schema=v3 that triggers the normalization shim; 4) telemetry tags on tool_choice decisions to measure how often schema normalization changes selection order. Migration plan: default remains v2; we enable v3 behind the header and a feature flag controlled by Canary routing. Rollback: toggle the feature flag or remove the header for callers. Tests: unit schema normalization tests, integration test that simulates slow fragments and validates heartbeat frames, and an e2e compatibility test with the openai-compat adapter. Implementation notes: normalization is conservative (no aggressive coercion), we add a stable mapping table for common aliases (int -> integer, str -> string, date-time -> string(format=date-time)), and a deterministic tool_choice tie-breaker that leverages schema specificity score + provenance weight. See related Linear items ENG-2981, ENG-3034. Checklist: [x] normalization pass implemented [x] streaming heartbeat implemented [x] unit + integration tests [x] docs updated [x] canary rollout configured

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Nit - can we rename 'heartbeat' -> 'ping-envelope' in code to avoid confusion with internal health checks? Priya: replied that heartbeat is already used in public docs for streaming keepalive and changing would be a bigger docs surgery; left as-is.

Maya Thompson: Request changes - normalization should not strip vendor extensions (x-*) from schema. Priya: updated implementation to copy vendor extensions into a provenance.header and added tests to assert they are preserved.

Luca Rinaldi: Concern about adding load under high QPS for the normalization pass. Priya: added micro-benchmarks (2x 1k req/s baseline) and an optional cache layer keyed by schema fingerprint; cache hits are expected to cover 70% of production traffic.
CI bot: integration pipeline flake on first run (timeout on test_stream_heartbeat). Priya: increased test timeout and added deterministic timing injection for the coalescer; CI passed on re-run.
release_notes: Adds OpenAI-Compat tool-schema v3 normalization and streaming heartbeat to avoid client timeouts during fragment coalescing. Opt-in via header OpenAI-Compat: tool-schema=v3. Improves tool_choice determinism and preserves vendor schema extensions in provenance metadata.
additional_notes: Performance: normalization introduces ~0.6ms median overhead on cold schema paths before caching. Telemetry: new tags openai_compat_schema_version and tool_choice_provenance added to choice metrics. Observability: dashboards updated under Observability > OpenAI-Compat.
